ios.desc:
Conquer the world starting from your single home city. Each city can build units (either tanks, planes, paratroopers, bombers, transports, destroyers, battleships, submarines or aircraft carriers) in order to explore the world and defeat the other five AI controlled enemy players.

There's a lot of AI in the computer's moves and the maps are randomly generated, so each game is interesting and challenging.

android.desc:
Fans of the old classic strategy wargame "Empire" will feel right at home with Mother Of All Battles where the object is to capture the world starting from your single home city. Each city can build units (either tanks, planes, paratroopers, bombers, transports, destroyers, battleships, submarines or aircraft carriers) in order to explore the world and defeat your enemies.

There's a lot of AI in the computer's moves and there are 260 maps to play on.

quotes.text: This for Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.windowsgames.moab or Windows: http://www.windowsgames.co.uk/mother.html ?

Ordered. Funnily enough I recently came across this GDC presentation by Sid and Bruce Shelley on the development of the original Civilization[0]. Highly recommended.

The influence of Empire as one of the inspirations of the game was obvious to anyone familiar with it. If you're interested there's an excellent updated implementation of Empire on the App Store[1]. I'd love to be able to get a version of Civ 2 on mobile. It's still by far my favourite iteration of Civ. Or Pirates!

[0]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJ-auWfJTts

[1]https://apps.apple.com/gb/app/mother-of-all-battles/id425160860

Check out this great GDC talk by Sid and Bruce on the history of the development of the game.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AJ-auWfJTts&t=3s

They mention Empire as an influence, and there's a really nice modern implementation of Empire available for Windows and iOS.
